target_customer: Car makers, mobility startups and engineering teams that buy an open electric vehicle platform and engineering services
problem: Building an electric vehicle prototype costs about $100k and years of R&D. Open Motors sold an open, modular platform that the YC post says could produce a prototype in under an hour.
business_model: Hardware platform sales (Tabby EVO) plus engineering and manufacturing services

founders.name: Tin Hang Liu
prior_employers: Italchina (family company helping Italian firms enter China)
founders.background_notes: Italian born per the YC page. A Wikipedia entry names a different founder spelling (Francisco Liu), a conflict noted below.

founders.name: Yuki Liu
founders.background_notes: From the YC blog post of 2016-03-18.

technical_complexity.rationale: A drivetrain and chassis platform (80V, 15 kW per Make magazine) that a buyer could assemble in about an hour required real automotive hardware engineering and supply chain work.

defensibility.rationale: The design was open source by intent, so copying was allowed, leaving brand and services as the only edge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The YC post named Ford and Chrysler as big brands able to afford vehicle R&D. No incumbent is documented as copying or buying the company; Renault reportedly used the platform to develop a concept car (search snippet, unverified).

market_need_then: The YC post (2016-03-18) argued that only large car brands could afford vehicle R&D and claimed savings of about $2M and three years of R&D from past projects. These are the company's claims.

branding.name_origin: OSVehicle (open source vehicle) was renamed Open Motors; Wikipedia says the rebrand was on the fourth anniversary in 2014, while another site says 8 December 2017. No source explains why.
branding.brand_signature: The 'IKEA car' and 'Arduino for Vehicles' labels attributed to media on the YC page

rebrands.why: Not stated; sources disagree on the date (2014 or December 2017)

branding.community_and_virality: Maker and open source coverage in Make magazine, Electrek and others; CAD files were released publicly.

brand_strength.rationale: Memorable media labels and maker press, but the company stayed small and the rebrand date is unclear.

pivots.to: Platform plus EDIT self-driving modular vehicle
pivots.why: Company announced EDIT as a self-driving vehicle for white label services (TechCrunch headline, 2017)

outcome_analysis: The reason for Open Motors' inactive YC status is not public: its own site still shows products, jobs and contact forms, so it may simply be small. It raised about $120K around YC and no larger round, acquisition or shutdown report was found. Failure factors stay empty because no source gives a cause.
notes: The $120K seed rests on databases (CB Insights, Wellfound; Dealroom says $125K). Claims that GM bought OSVehicle for about $1 billion appear only on low authority sites and are rejected. Wikipedia names founder Francisco Liu and engineer Ampelio Macchi; the YC page says Tin Hang Liu, a conflict not resolved. The pivot date comes from a TechCrunch headline seen only in a search result. No dated competitor rival was found (Local Motors appears only in a 2017 article, too late), so the list is empty. Site shows no dates so current operation is unconfirmed.
